docs/execution/rulings/R-003-the-verifier-is-not-traced-by-itself.md
     1	---
     2	id: R-003
     3	attack_class: corpus leakage
     4	target: crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs:1
     5	claim_requires: does not run under strace; the verifier itself
     6	claim_excludes: chdir; fchdir; dirfd; renameat; wrote; write access
     7	status: ruled
     8	ruled_by: Brian
     9	date: 2026-09-08
    10	---
    11	
    12	# R-003 — the verifier is not traced by itself
    13	
    14	**Finding ruled on.** Blind pass 2 at lane base `5fb1b57`, attempt A07 (corpus
    15	leakage): "`verify_inventory_repo` does not run under strace and the corpus
    16	access audit only covers the qualification lane stages, not the verifier
    17	itself."
    18	
    19	**True as stated.** The eight scope traces cover the lane's stages. The
    20	verifier that judges those traces runs outside them.
    21	
    22	**Ruling.** This is class C under AM-17.9: closing it requires the gate to be
    23	its own adversary. Tracing the verifier under the lane's own tracer would
    24	produce a trace the same verifier judges, so a verifier that wanted to hide a
    25	locked-corpus read would simply not report it — the check would grow, the
    26	assurance would not. The one-tracer constraint (F-43) also forbids nesting the
    27	stage tracer inside itself.
    28	
    29	What the campaign has instead is external: the verifier is tracked source at a
    30	fixed commit, every change to it passes through a reviewed commit, and the
    31	reviewers are given `haq.rs` in full precisely so a human-independent party
    32	reads what the gate does. The residual — that a hostile author of the gate
    33	could read the locked corpus from inside the gate — is stated, not closed.
    34	
    35	**Effect.** This ruling can clear only the claim at the exact persisted target
    36	`crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs:1`, if its class and claim phrases match. It
    37	does not clear another claim, a stage trace, a directory fd, a `chdir`, or a
    38	write to the locked corpus.

    28	in-tree partial answer — the mutation campaign that found twenty-seven
    29	verifier functions surviving replacement with `Ok(())` — and it measures
    30	accident, not malice.

docs/execution/rulings/R-006-a-per-file-census-has-no-order-to-drift.md
     1	---
     2	id: R-006
     3	attack_class: nondeterminism
     4	target: crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs:2847
     5	claim_requires: compares counts not order
     6	claim_excludes: spawn; thread; concurrent; pthread; async
     7	status: ruled
     8	ruled_by: Brian
     9	date: 2026-09-08
    10	---
    11	
    12	# R-006 — a per-file census has no order to drift
    13	
    14	**Finding ruled INCORRECT.** Blind pass 2 at lane base `5fb1b57`, attempt A06
    15	(nondeterminism): "the durable surface measurement compares counts not order
    16	and the scope check uses `BTreeMap` for declared surface so ordering drift is
    17	not detected by the current gate."
    18	
    19	**The measurement has no order to lose.** `durable_transition_sites` returns a
    20	map from file path to the number of durable transitions that file performs, and
    21	`crash_boundary_scope` declares the same shape. Reordering two `commit_if`
    22	calls inside one file changes neither which files perform durable transitions
    23	nor how many each performs, so there is no drift for the check to miss. A
    24	`BTreeMap` is the right structure precisely because the census is a set of
    25	(path, count) facts and its iteration order is then deterministic.
    26	
    27	The cited coordinate does not carry the claim either: `haq.rs:2847` in that
    28	tree is a doc comment about mutant kill attribution and Phase 1 test
    29	quarantine.
    30	
    31	If ordering ever becomes load-bearing — a boundary sequence whose ORDER is the
    32	invariant, as ILRP's eight protocol steps are — that is a different surface with
    33	a different check, and this ruling does not reach it.
    34	
    35	**Effect.** This ruling can clear only the claim at the exact persisted target
    36	`crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs:2847`, if its class and claim phrases match.
    37	It does not clear another claim about spawned threads or concurrent execution.

     2	id: R-007
     3	attack_class: weak mutants
     4	target: conformance/haqp/packet.json:1652
     5	claim_requires: killing tests

     7	status: ruled

    10	---
    11	
    12	# R-007 — whether a named killer kills its mutant is measured at M24, not asserted at M17.5
    13	
    14	**Recorded by Brian on 2026-09-30.** This exact-coordinate ruling takes effect
    15	only after its commit verifies against `conformance/haqp/ruling-signers`.
    16	
    17	**Finding ruled on.** Blind pass 1 at lane base `cbed339f`, attempt A04 (weak
    18	mutants): "Mutant at conformance/haqp/packet.json:1652 names formatter-focused
    19	P1-T18 and P1-T19, neither of which exercises changed jurisdiction threshold
    20	behavior."
    21	
    22	**What is true.** P1-M042 shifts a threshold in
    23	`crates/liminal-jurisdiction/src/checker.rs`, and its killers are M20 `lim fmt`
    24	tests. They are derived by AM-17.10's rule from the requirement the mutant
    25	defends, P1-R015 (D20.3: `lim fmt` replaces governed Holders atomically). That
    26	path runs through the jurisdiction checker, which is why the mutant is mapped
    27	there.
    28	
    29	**Why it is not fixable in this stage.** P1-T18 and P1-T19 do not exist.
    30	AM-17.4 defers every Phase 1 test, and ADR-0021 moves ADR-0020 §3's mutation
    31	clauses to HAQP-1b at M24. Whether a test that is not yet written exercises a
    32	threshold is exactly what that campaign measures, by running the mutant.
    33	Re-mapping by judgment now would replace the derived rule with an unmeasured
    34	guess. This is RISK-001, and the F-74 A02 precedent (RISK-007): a claim about
    35	the strength of tests AM-17.4 says are unwritten.
    36

    38	`conformance/haqp/packet.json:1652`, if its class and claim phrases match. It
    39	does not clear a claim about a disposition, a kill, a `not-ready` row, or an
    40	anchor or coordinate. Those are defects in the packet as it stands, and are
    41	excluded by name.
docs/execution/rulings/R-008-a-ruling-answers-a-claim-within-its-file.md
     1	---
     2	id: R-008
     3	attack_class: exception broadening
     4	target: crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs:3166
     5	claim_requires: ruling target
     6	claim_excludes: signature; signer; unsigned; draft; status
     7	status: withdrawn
     8	ruled_by: Brian
     9	date: 2026-09-30
    10	---
    11	
    12	# R-008 — a file-scoped ruling is RISK-004, disclosed, not a defect
    13	
    14	**Withdrawn by Brian on 2026-09-30.** The file-wide scope is rejected. This
    15	record is retained as an audit artifact and never clears a finding.
    16	
    17	**Finding ruled on.** Blind pass 1 at lane base `cbed339f`, attempt A08
    18	(exception broadening): "Branch at crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs:3166 accepts
    19	whole-file target plus substring phrase matches, bypassing required
    20	exact-coordinate exception scope."
    21	
    22	**What is true.** A ruling whose `target` names a file, not a coordinate, clears
    23	a matching claim anywhere in that file, and the claim is matched by required
    24	and excluded phrases. That is RISK-004 verbatim: "a standing ruling can clear a
    25	finding it does not answer: whether two sentences describe one claim is not
    26	decidable from the sentences." AM-17.15 keeps RISK-004 recorded, because it is
    27	the qualifier reasoning about its own findings.
    28	
    29	**Why file scope is intended.** R-001..R-006 rule on classes of claim that
    30	recur anywhere in `haq.rs` (stage reads of the corpus, a gate not catching its
    31	own change), and a coordinate goes stale with every edit to the file. The
    32	existing mitigations stay: a coordinate-scoped ruling is held to its
    33	coordinate, a ruling clears at most one attempt per record, and excluded
    34	phrases carve out neighbouring claims. Requiring coordinates for every ruling
    35	would retire R-001..R-006 and force each to be re-signed at a coordinate that
    36	moves.
    37	
    38	**Effect.** A verified finding of class `exception broadening` on
    39	`crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs` whose claim is that a ruling's file-scoped
    40	target and phrase matching clear claims outside its intended scope is cleared
    41	while this ruling is `ruled`. It does not clear a claim about signatures,
    42	signers, drafts or status. Those are the controls that keep a ruling Brian's,
    43	and are excluded by name.

  1016	/// Judge each boundary's observed terminals against the protocol's table.
  1017	fn verify_crash_terminal_states(evidence: &CrashEvidence) -> Result<()> {

  1019	        let expected = CRASH_TERMINAL_EXPECTATION
  1020	            .iter()
  1021	            .find(|(boundary, _)| *boundary == row.boundary)
  1022	            .map(|(_, states)| *states)
  1023	            .with_context(|| {
  1024	                format!(
  1025	                    "crash boundary {:?} has no declared terminal expectation; a boundary the \
  1026	                     protocol table does not name cannot be judged",
  1027	                    row.boundary
  1028	                )
  1029	            })?;
  1030	        for pair in &row.recovery_pairs {
  1031	            anyhow::ensure!(
  1032	                pair.first_terminals == expected,
  1033	                "crash boundary {} recovered to {:?} in scenario {} occurrence {}; the protocol \
  1034	                 requires {expected:?}",
  1035	                row.boundary,
  1036	                pair.first_terminals,
  1037	                pair.scenario,
  1038	                pair.occurrence
  1039	            );
  1040	        }
  1041	    }
  1042	    let named = CRASH_TERMINAL_EXPECTATION
  1043	        .iter()
  1044	        .map(|(boundary, _)| (*boundary).to_owned())
  1045	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
  1046	    let recorded = evidence
  1047	        .boundaries
  1048	        .iter()
  1049	        .map(|row| row.boundary.clone())
  1050	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
  1051	    anyhow::ensure!(
  1052	        named == recorded,
  1053	        "crash boundaries recorded {recorded:?} but the protocol table names {named:?}"

  1055	    Ok(())
  1056	}

   909	    verify_markdown_tables(root, &packet)?;
   910	    verify_oracle_independence(root)?;

   912	        "qualification_state",

   914	        "complete",
   915	    )?;

   918	        &packet,

   921	            // disposition is stage-dependent. Hardcoding `killed` here made
   922	            // HAQP-1a UNREACHABLE: leave mutants `predeclared` and this gate
   923	            // failed; mark one `killed` and verify_qualification_stage failed.
   924	            // The first version of ADR-0021 shipped with exactly that
   925	            // contradiction — the deadlock it existed to break, reintroduced
   926	            // one layer down.
   927	            mutant: if packet.qualification_stage == "1b" {
   928	                "resolved"
   929	            } else {
   930	                "predeclared"
   931	            },

   984	/// Bind the packet's crash-boundary claims to the fault lane's committed
   985	/// artifact (M17.5 pass-2 #19).
   986	///
   987	/// The lane wrote `target/haqp/crash.json`, which is gitignored, so nothing
   988	/// could ever read it back: the artifact said `pass`, the packet said
   989	/// `registered`, and `haq verify-inventory` exited 0 with no one comparing the
   990	/// two. The packet's crash rows were pure assertion.
   991	/// What ILRP recovery must reach from each registered crash boundary, read off
   992	/// the protocol rather than off the run. Blind pass 1 at `6b36bbb9` (A06): the
   993	/// evidence carried digests, which prove recovery is repeatable and leaves no
   994	/// residue and cannot say WHICH state it repeatably reached, and the only
   995	/// terminal expectation was one string declared by the scenario the harness
   996	/// itself runs. A recovery resolving every boundary wrongly but consistently
   997	/// satisfied all of it.
   998	///
   999	/// The protocol decides these, not the implementation: before the intent is
  1000	/// durable there is nothing to recover, so recovery must find no terminal at
  1001	/// all; once it is durable the protocol rolls forward, so every later boundary
  1002	/// must reach `Committed`. A boundary reaching anything else — `Aborted` after
  1003	/// the intent was committed, or `NeedsReview` where the world was intact — is
  1004	/// a recovery that lost or invented work.
  1005	const CRASH_TERMINAL_EXPECTATION: [(&str, &[&str]); 8] = [
  1006	    ("ilrp/before_intent_commit", &[]),
  1007	    ("ilrp/after_intent_commit", &["Committed"]),
  1008	    ("ilrp/before_external_apply", &["Committed"]),
  1009	    ("ilrp/after_external_apply", &["Committed"]),
  1010	    ("ilrp/before_ack", &["Committed"]),
  1011	    ("ilrp/after_ack", &["Committed"]),
  1012	    ("ilrp/before_finalize", &["Committed"]),
  1013	    ("ilrp/after_finalize_before_notify", &["Committed"]),
  1014	];

  1016	/// Judge each boundary's observed terminals against the protocol's table.
  1017	fn verify_crash_terminal_states(evidence: &CrashEvidence) -> Result<()> {
  1018	    for row in &evidence.boundaries {
  1019	        let expected = CRASH_TERMINAL_EXPECTATION
  1020	            .iter()
  1021	            .find(|(boundary, _)| *boundary == row.boundary)
  1022	            .map(|(_, states)| *states)
  1023	            .with_context(|| {
  1024	                format!(
  1025	                    "crash boundary {:?} has no declared terminal expectation; a boundary the \
  1026	                     protocol table does not name cannot be judged",
  1027	                    row.boundary
  1028	                )
  1029	            })?;
  1030	        for pair in &row.recovery_pairs {
  1031	            anyhow::ensure!(
  1032	                pair.first_terminals == expected,
  1033	                "crash boundary {} recovered to {:?} in scenario {} occurrence {}; the protocol \
  1034	                 requires {expected:?}",
  1035	                row.boundary,
  1036	                pair.first_terminals,
  1037	                pair.scenario,
  1038	                pair.occurrence
  1039	            );
  1040	        }
  1041	    }
  1042	    let named = CRASH_TERMINAL_EXPECTATION
  1043	        .iter()
  1044	        .map(|(boundary, _)| (*boundary).to_owned())
  1045	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
  1046	    let recorded = evidence
  1047	        .boundaries
  1048	        .iter()
  1049	        .map(|row| row.boundary.clone())
  1050	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
  1051	    anyhow::ensure!(
  1052	        named == recorded,
  1053	        "crash boundaries recorded {recorded:?} but the protocol table names {named:?}"
  1054	    );
  1055	    Ok(())
  1056	}

  1244	fn verify_canary_rows(declared: &[Canary], recorded: &[CanaryEvidence]) -> Result<()> {
  1245	    require_unique(
  1246	        recorded.iter().map(|row| row.id.as_str()),
  1247	        "canary evidence",
  1248	    )?;
  1249	    let by_id: BTreeMap<&str, &CanaryEvidence> =
  1250	        recorded.iter().map(|row| (row.id.as_str(), row)).collect();
  1251	    for canary in declared {
  1252	        if canary.result != "caught" {
  1253	            continue;
  1254	        }
  1255	        let evidence = by_id.get(canary.id.as_str()).with_context(|| {
  1256	            format!(
  1257	                "{} claims caught but the committed canary run has no such canary",
  1258	                canary.id
  1259	            )
  1260	        })?;
  1261	        if !evidence.caught {
  1262	            anyhow::bail!(
  1263	                "{} claims caught but the committed run recorded it as NOT caught",
  1264	                canary.id
  1265	            );
  1266	        }
  1267	        // The prose must describe the mutation that actually ran, or the table
  1268	        // a reader trusts describes a different experiment from the one
  1269	        // performed.
  1270	        if evidence.violation != canary.violation {
  1271	            anyhow::bail!(
  1272	                "{}: packet says the violation is {:?} but the run performed {:?}",
  1273	                canary.id,
  1274	                canary.violation,
  1275	                evidence.violation
  1276	            );
  1277	        }
  1278	        if evidence.expected_failure != canary.expected_failure {
  1279	            anyhow::bail!(
  1280	                "{}: packet expects failure {:?} but the run expected {:?}",
  1281	                canary.id,
  1282	                canary.expected_failure,
  1283	                evidence.expected_failure
  1284	            );
  1285	        }
  1286	        anyhow::ensure!(
  1287	            canary_failure_matches(&evidence.expected_failure, &evidence.observed_failure),
  1288	            "{}: observed failure {:?} does not match expected failure {:?}",
  1289	            canary.id,
  1290	            evidence.observed_failure,
  1291	            evidence.expected_failure

  1016	/// Judge each boundary's observed terminals against the protocol's table.
  1017	fn verify_crash_terminal_states(evidence: &CrashEvidence) -> Result<()> {
  1018	    for row in &evidence.boundaries {
  1019	        let expected = CRASH_TERMINAL_EXPECTATION
  1020	            .iter()
  1021	            .find(|(boundary, _)| *boundary == row.boundary)
  1022	            .map(|(_, states)| *states)
  1023	            .with_context(|| {
  1024	                format!(
  1025	                    "crash boundary {:?} has no declared terminal expectation; a boundary the \
  1026	                     protocol table does not name cannot be judged",
  1027	                    row.boundary
  1028	                )
  1029	            })?;
  1030	        for pair in &row.recovery_pairs {
  1031	            anyhow::ensure!(
  1032	                pair.first_terminals == expected,
  1033	                "crash boundary {} recovered to {:?} in scenario {} occurrence {}; the protocol \
  1034	                 requires {expected:?}",
  1035	                row.boundary,
  1036	                pair.first_terminals,
  1037	                pair.scenario,
  1038	                pair.occurrence
  1039	            );
  1040	        }
  1041	    }
  1042	    let named = CRASH_TERMINAL_EXPECTATION
  1043	        .iter()
  1044	        .map(|(boundary, _)| (*boundary).to_owned())
  1045	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
  1046	    let recorded = evidence
  1047	        .boundaries
  1048	        .iter()
  1049	        .map(|row| row.boundary.clone())
  1050	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
  1051	    anyhow::ensure!(
  1052	        named == recorded,
  1053	        "crash boundaries recorded {recorded:?} but the protocol table names {named:?}"
  1054	    );
  1055	    Ok(())
  1056	}

3590	/// Before this, a receipt naming any command with a self-authored
  3591	/// `verification_exit_code: 0` was accepted without the command ever being
  3592	/// executed — the resolution asserted its own success. The command is drawn
  3593	/// from a closed registry rather than run as written: executing arbitrary text
  3594	/// out of an evidence file would hand whoever wrote the file this process.
  3595	const RESOLUTION_COMMANDS: [(&str, &[&str]); 4] = [
  3596	    ("just ci", &["just", "ci"]),
  3597	    ("just haq-inventory", &["just", "haq-inventory"]),
  3598	    ("just haq-canaries", &["just", "haq-canaries"]),
  3599	    (
  3600	        "cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features",
  3601	        &["cargo", "nextest", "run", "--workspace", "--all-features"],
  3602	    ),
  3603	];
  3604	
  3605	/// The registry's commands are the project's own gates, run with the gate's
  3606	/// environment and no timeout: they are what CI runs, so a hang here is a hang
  3607	/// in CI, visible either way (review of `e490671`). The working directory is a
  3608	/// disposable worktree at the commit the receipt names, never the live tree.
  3609	fn verify_resolution_command_ran(
  3610	    root: &Utf8Path,
  3611	    who: &str,
  3612	    evidence_text: &str,
  3613	    commit: &str,
  3614	) -> Result<()> {
  3615	    let claimed = evidence_text
  3616	        .lines()
  3617	        .find_map(|line| line.trim_start().strip_prefix("verification_command:"))
  3618	        .map(str::trim)
  3619	        .unwrap_or_default();
  3620	    let argv = RESOLUTION_COMMANDS
  3621	        .iter()
  3622	        .find(|(name, _)| *name == claimed)
  3623	        .map(|(_, argv)| *argv)
  3624	        .with_context(|| {
  3625	            format!(
  3626	                "{who}: resolution claims verification command {claimed:?}, which is not one the \
  3627	                 gate can run; the registry is closed so a receipt cannot name a command that \
  3628	                 exists only in its own text"
  3629	            )
  3630	        })?;
  3631	    let (program, rest) = argv.split_first().context("registry command is empty")?;
  3632	    // Blind pass 1 at aecb2ec7 (A12): the command ran against the working
  3633	    // tree, so a receipt claiming a finding was resolved at some commit was
  3634	    // answered by whether the command passes at HEAD. Reachability was
  3635	    // checked and the commit then ignored. It runs in a disposable worktree
  3636	    // checked out at the claimed commit now, which is what the receipt says.
  3637	    let scratch = liminal_scratch::ScratchDir::new("haq-resolution-replay")?;
  3638	    let worktree = scratch.path().to_owned();
  3639	    let add = Command::new("git")
  3640	        .current_dir(root)
  3641	        .args(["worktree", "add", "--detach", "--quiet"])
  3642	        .arg(&worktree)
  3643	        .arg(commit)
  3644	        .output()?;

  4566	    ("broadened-allow-list", "negative"),

  4581	/// The killing tests AM-17.10 derives for `mutant`: the candidates are the
  4582	/// tests the packet maps to its requirement, in packet order; the primary is
  4583	/// the first candidate observed the way this operator shows itself; the
  4584	/// secondary is the first remaining candidate of a different evidence kind.
  4585	/// Each fallback is to the next candidate, never outside the requirement.
  4586	fn derive_killing_tests(packet: &Packet, mutant: &Mutant) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
  4587	    // Position among the mutants sharing this requirement. F-05 caps any one
  4588	    // test at a quarter of the plan, and a rule that always picked the first
  4589	    // apt candidate put P1-T07 on 46% of it. Rotation spreads the claim across
  4590	    // the tests that defend the requirement instead of piling it on the first.
  4591	    let ordinal = packet
  4592	        .mutants
  4593	        .iter()
  4594	        .take_while(|other| other.id != mutant.id)
  4595	        .filter(|other| other.requirement == mutant.requirement)
  4596	        .count();
  4597	    let observed = MUTANT_OBSERVATION_KIND
  4598	        .iter()
  4599	        .find(|(operator, _)| *operator == mutant.operator)
  4600	        .map(|(_, kind)| *kind)
  4601	        .with_context(|| {
  4602	            format!(
  4603	                "{} carries operator {:?}, which names no observation kind; AM-17.10 requires \
  4604	                 one before the plan can carry the operator",
  4605	                mutant.id, mutant.operator
  4606	            )
  4607	        })?;

  4609	        .tests
  4610	        .iter()
  4611	        .filter(|test| test.requirements.contains(&mutant.requirement))
  4612	        .collect();
  4613	    anyhow::ensure!(
  4614	        candidates.len() >= 2,
  4615	        "{} names requirement {}, which {} test(s) defend; a pair of killers needs two",
  4616	        mutant.id,
  4617	        mutant.requirement,
  4618	        candidates.len()
  4619	    );
  4620	    let observed_candidates: Vec<&&Test> = candidates
  4621	        .iter()
  4622	        .filter(|test| test.evidence.iter().any(|kind| kind == observed))
  4623	        .collect();
  4624	    // Rotation applies whether or not the operator's kind is available: the
  4625	    // fallback candidate list is still a list, and taking its head every time
  4626	    // is what put one test on 46% of the plan (review of `95a97b8b`).
  4627	    let primary = if observed_candidates.is_empty() {
  4628	        candidates[ordinal % candidates.len()]
  4629	    } else {
  4630	        observed_candidates[ordinal % observed_candidates.len()]
  4631	    };
  4632	    let start = candidates
  4633	        .iter()
  4634	        .position(|test| test.id == primary.id)
  4635	        .context("the primary is one of the candidates")?;
  4636	    let after = |step: usize| candidates[(start + step) % candidates.len()];
  4637	    let secondary = (1..candidates.len())
  4638	        .map(after)
  4639	        .find(|test| test.evidence != primary.evidence)
  4640	        .unwrap_or_else(|| after(1));

  4642	}

  4545	///
  4546	/// ADR-0020 §4 wants at least 64 semantic mutants at a 100% kill rate. The
  4547	/// packet declares 65, each naming the tests that would catch it — and as of
  4548	/// 2026-08-03 **not one of those 35 distinct tests is runnable**: 27 exist only
  4549	/// as strings in the packet (M18–M24 have not been authorized, so
  4550	/// `conformance/tests/milestones/` has no m18..m24 at all), and the remaining 8
  4551	/// exist but are `#[ignore]`d under the AM-17.2 Phase 1 quarantine.
  4552	///
  4553	/// A kill demonstrated by a test that does not exist is not demonstrated. A
  4554	/// kill demonstrated by a test nobody runs is not demonstrated either — an
  4555	/// `#[ignore]`d test cannot fail, so it cannot witness anything.
  4556	///
  4557	/// This check exists so that gap cannot be closed by editing dispositions to
  4558	/// `killed`. It is deliberately unsatisfiable today, and that is the correct
  4559	/// state: the mutation requirement is GATED on the Phase 1 milestones writing
  4560	/// their tests, not on anything M17.5 can produce.
  4561	/// How each mutation operator is observed. AM-17.10: a killer is derived, not
  4562	/// declared, and the primary killer is the test whose evidence kind is the way
  4563	/// this operator's defect shows itself. Closed table — a new operator must
  4564	/// name its observation here before the plan can carry it.
  4565	const MUTANT_OBSERVATION_KIND: [(&str, &str); 13] = [
  4566	    ("broadened-allow-list", "negative"),
  4567	    ("disabled-crash-point", "recovery"),
  4568	    ("missing-enum-dispatch", "malformed"),
  4569	    ("oracle-short-circuit", "positive"),
  4570	    ("ordering-nondeterminism", "replay"),
  4571	    ("predicate-deletion", "positive"),
  4572	    ("predicate-inversion", "negative"),
  4573	    ("skipped-durable-transition", "recovery"),
  4574	    ("stale-basis-acceptance", "basis"),
  4575	    ("success-error-substitution", "negative"),
  4576	    ("threshold-minus-one", "malformed"),
  4577	    ("threshold-plus-one", "malformed"),
  4578	    ("wrong-holder-selection", "basis"),
  4579	];

  4581	/// The killing tests AM-17.10 derives for `mutant`: the candidates are the
  4582	/// tests the packet maps to its requirement, in packet order; the primary is
  4583	/// the first candidate observed the way this operator shows itself; the
  4584	/// secondary is the first remaining candidate of a different evidence kind.
  4585	/// Each fallback is to the next candidate, never outside the requirement.
  4586	fn derive_killing_tests(packet: &Packet, mutant: &Mutant) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
  4587	    // Position among the mutants sharing this requirement. F-05 caps any one
  4588	    // test at a quarter of the plan, and a rule that always picked the first
  4589	    // apt candidate put P1-T07 on 46% of it. Rotation spreads the claim across
  4590	    // the tests that defend the requirement instead of piling it on the first.
  4591	    let ordinal = packet
  4592	        .mutants
  4593	        .iter()
  4594	        .take_while(|other| other.id != mutant.id)
  4595	        .filter(|other| other.requirement == mutant.requirement)
  4596	        .count();
  4597	    let observed = MUTANT_OBSERVATION_KIND
  4598	        .iter()
  4599	        .find(|(operator, _)| *operator == mutant.operator)
  4600	        .map(|(_, kind)| *kind)
  4601	        .with_context(|| {
  4602	            format!(
  4603	                "{} carries operator {:?}, which names no observation kind; AM-17.10 requires \
  4604	                 one before the plan can carry the operator",
  4605	                mutant.id, mutant.operator
  4606	            )
  4607	        })?;
  4608	    let candidates: Vec<&Test> = packet
  4609	        .tests
  4610	        .iter()
  4611	        .filter(|test| test.requirements.contains(&mutant.requirement))
  4612	        .collect();
  4613	    anyhow::ensure!(
  4614	        candidates.len() >= 2,
  4615	        "{} names requirement {}, which {} test(s) defend; a pair of killers needs two",
  4616	        mutant.id,
  4617	        mutant.requirement,
  4618	        candidates.len()
  4619	    );
  4620	    let observed_candidates: Vec<&&Test> = candidates
  4621	        .iter()
  4622	        .filter(|test| test.evidence.iter().any(|kind| kind == observed))
  4623	        .collect();
  4624	    // Rotation applies whether or not the operator's kind is available: the
  4625	    // fallback candidate list is still a list, and taking its head every time
  4626	    // is what put one test on 46% of the plan (review of `95a97b8b`).
  4627	    let primary = if observed_candidates.is_empty() {
  4628	        candidates[ordinal % candidates.len()]
  4629	    } else {
  4630	        observed_candidates[ordinal % observed_candidates.len()]
  4631	    };
  4632	    let start = candidates
  4633	        .iter()
  4634	        .position(|test| test.id == primary.id)
  4635	        .context("the primary is one of the candidates")?;
  4636	    let after = |step: usize| candidates[(start + step) % candidates.len()];
  4637	    let secondary = (1..candidates.len())
  4638	        .map(after)
  4639	        .find(|test| test.evidence != primary.evidence)
  4640	        .unwrap_or_else(|| after(1));
  4641	    Ok(vec![primary.id.clone(), secondary.id.clone()])
  4642	}

  4661	/// The campaign's first blind-review lane. A coordinate whose line was last
  4662	/// changed at or after this commit is the qualifier's own churn rather than
  4663	/// the suite under qualification (AM-17.11).
  4664	const CAMPAIGN_FIRST_LANE: &str = "0d8c32a4ae1afda9808e55c3c291445aad4e3d60";
  4665	
  4666	/// Whether `coordinate` — a `file:line` a finding names — points at a line
  4667	/// this campaign wrote. Answered from `git blame`, so the classification that
  4668	/// decides whether a finding is fixed or recorded is evidence rather than the
  4669	/// qualifier's judgement about its own work.
  4670	pub fn coordinate_is_campaign_churn(root: &Utf8Path, coordinate: &str) -> Result<bool> {
  4671	    let (file, line) = coordinate
  4672	        .rsplit_once(':')
  4673	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate:?} is not a file:line coordinate"))?;
  4674	    let line: u32 = line
  4675	        .parse()
  4676	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate:?} does not name a line"))?;
  4677	    anyhow::ensure!(line > 0, "{coordinate:?} names line zero");
  4678	    let blamed = git_text(
  4679	        root,
  4680	        &[
  4681	            "blame",
  4682	            "--porcelain",
  4683	            "-L",
  4684	            &format!("{line},{line}"),
  4685	            "--",
  4686	            file,
  4687	        ],
  4688	    )
  4689	    .with_context(|| format!("blame {coordinate}"))?;
  4690	    let commit = blamed
  4691	        .split_whitespace()
  4692	        .next()
  4693	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate}: blame named no commit"))?;
  4694	    // `merge-base --is-ancestor A B` succeeds when A is an ancestor of B. The
  4695	    // campaign's first lane being an ancestor of the blamed commit means the
  4696	    // line was written during the campaign.
  4697	    let status = Command::new("git")
  4698	        .current_dir(root)
  4699	        .args(["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", CAMPAIGN_FIRST_LANE, commit])
  4700	        .status()
  4701	        .context("git merge-base --is-ancestor")?;
  4702	    Ok(status.success())
  4703	}

  4705	fn verify_mutant_killing_tests(root: &Utf8Path, packet: &Packet) -> Result<()> {
  4706	    // AM-17.10: the column is derived for every mutant, whatever its
  4707	    // disposition, and is checked before the clauses that inspect only killed
  4708	    // ones. This function used to return here when nothing was killed, so at
  4709	    // stage 1a — where all 65 mutants are predeclared — it read nothing at
  4710	    // all, and a generated killer column rode through fourteen lanes.
  4711	    let killed: Vec<&Mutant> = packet
  4712	        .mutants
  4713	        .iter()
  4714	        .filter(|mutant| mutant.disposition == "killed")
  4715	        .collect();
  4716	    let by_id: BTreeMap<&str, &Test> = packet
  4717	        .tests
  4718	        .iter()
  4719	        .map(|test| (test.id.as_str(), test))
  4720	        .collect();
  4721	    let ignored = ignored_test_names(root);
  4722	    for mutant in killed {
  4723	        if mutant.killing_tests.is_empty() {
  4724	            anyhow::bail!("{} claims killed but names no killing test", mutant.id);
  4725	        }
  4726	        for test_id in &mutant.killing_tests {
  4727	            let test = by_id.get(test_id.as_str()).with_context(|| {
  4728	                format!(
  4729	                    "{} names killing test {test_id}, which the packet does not declare",
  4730	                    mutant.id
  4731	                )
  4732	            })?;
  4733	            let leaf = test.name.rsplit("::").next().unwrap_or(test.name.as_str());
  4734	            if ignored.contains(leaf) {
  4735	                anyhow::bail!(
  4736	                    "{} claims killed by {} ({}), which is #[ignore]d — an ignored test \
  4737	                     never runs, so it cannot witness a kill",
  4738	                    mutant.id,
  4739	                    test_id,
  4740	                    test.name
  4741	                );
  4742	            }
  4743	        }
  4744	    }
  4745	    // AM-17.10: every mutant's column is derived, whatever its disposition.
  4746	    // Checked last so a kill witnessed by an ignored or missing test reports
  4747	    // that, rather than being answered by the derivation. The clauses above
  4748	    // inspect only `killed` mutants, which is why a plan of 65 predeclared
  4749	    // mutants carried a generated killer column through fourteen lanes with
  4750	    // no gate reading it at all.
  4751	    for mutant in &packet.mutants {
  4752	        let derived = derive_killing_tests(packet, mutant)?;
  4753	        anyhow::ensure!(
  4754	            mutant.killing_tests == derived,
  4755	            "{} names killing tests {:?}; AM-17.10 derives {:?} from requirement {} and \
  4756	             operator {:?}",
  4757	            mutant.id,
  4758	            mutant.killing_tests,
  4759	            derived,
  4760	            mutant.requirement,
  4761	            mutant.operator
  4762	        );
  4763	    }
  4764	    Ok(())
  4765	}

  5047	                row.id,

  7313	/// Verify each scope's CAPTURED trace, rather than re-running the campaign.
  7314	///
  7315	/// This used to re-execute every scope's lane command inside a worktree —
  7316	/// `just ci`, `haq generate --cases 100000`, `cargo test --workspace`,
  7317	/// `just haq-blind-review` and `scripts/haqp_fuzz_campaign.sh 1800`. That made
  7318	/// `haq-verify` a second complete campaign, with a second fuzz run and a second
  7319	/// pair of paid model reviews inside every lane, and it threatened §7's
  7320	/// eight-hour ceiling with work that produced no new evidence.
  7321	///
  7322	/// It had never fired: `scope_traces` was empty, so the loop body never ran.
  7323	/// Populating it — which `verify_corpus_scope_presence` requires — would have
  7324	/// switched it on.
  7325	///

  7327	/// lane captures each scope under strace as it actually runs, and the gate
  7328	/// checks the recorded bytes: the command matches the closed lane registry, the
  7329	/// path digest matches, no stage wrote to the repository's locked corpus and no
  7330	/// carved fuzz binary touched it at all (F-44 ruling, 2026-09-05), and every
  7331	/// traced corpus path resolves inside the tree. What is lost is the reproducibility claim that
  7332	/// re-execution made; what is gained is evidence describing the run that
  7333	/// happened rather than a different one.
  7334	fn verify_corpus_scope_replays(
  7335	    root: &Utf8Path,
  7336	    rows: &[CorpusScopeTrace],
  7337	    targets: &[CorpusAccessAuditTarget],

  7339	    for row in rows {
  7340	        let expected_command = format!(
  7341	            "strace -f -q -e trace=%file -o target/haqp/scope-{}.trace {}",
  7342	            row.scope,
  7343	            scope_lane_command(&row.scope)?
  7344	        );

  7346	            &format!("{} corpus scope command", row.scope),
  7347	            &row.command,
  7348	            &expected_command,
  7349	        )?;
  7350	        verify_scope_trace_parts(row, targets)?;
  7351	        let (remainder, open, forbidden) = scan_scope_trace_union(root, row)?;
  7352	        if let Some(fragment) = forbidden {
  7353	            anyhow::bail!(
  7354	                "{} corpus scope trace opened a locked path ({fragment})",
  7355	                row.scope
  7356	            );
  7357	        }
  7358	        let label = format!("{} corpus scope", row.scope);

  7565	/// The path arguments of one traced file syscall, lexical, as strace printed
  7566	/// them, each with whether the call can change what the path names (F-44).
  7567	/// Two-path syscalls yield both strings; a symlink's target counts as written
  7568	/// because a link INTO the locked corpus is the second-name attack. strace
  7569	/// prints one syscall per line, so the earliest needle is the line's call.
  7570	fn scope_trace_line_accesses(line: &str) -> Vec<(String, bool)> {
  7571	    scope_trace_line_arguments(line)
  7572	        .into_iter()
  7573	        .map(|(path, write, _)| (path, write))
  7574	        .collect()

  7577	/// Whether strace reported a failed syscall. Inspect only the return-value
  7578	/// delimiter after the final syscall close, so a valid filename containing
  7579	/// the text ` = -1 ` cannot masquerade as an `ENOENT` result.
  7580	fn scope_trace_line_failed(line: &str) -> bool {
  7581	    line.rfind(") = ")
  7582	        .and_then(|index| line[index + 4..].split_whitespace().next())
  7583	        .is_some_and(|value| value == "-1")
  7584	}

  7586	/// The same, plus the directory fd each path was resolved against: the nearest
  7587	/// preceding bare integer argument, `None` for `AT_FDCWD` and for calls that
  7588	/// take no dirfd. Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A10, A11): only `openat`'s FIRST
  7589	/// argument was read, so `renameat`'s destination dirfd was ignored and a
  7590	/// descriptor opened without `O_DIRECTORY` was dropped from the map entirely.
  7591	fn scope_trace_line_arguments(line: &str) -> Vec<(String, bool, Option<i64>)> {
  7592	    let Some((open, needle)) = FILE_SYSCALLS
  7593	        .into_iter()
  7594	        .filter_map(|needle| line.find(needle).map(|index| (index, needle)))
  7595	        .min_by_key(|(index, _)| *index)
  7596	    else {
  7597	        return Vec::new();
  7598	    };
  7599	    let rest = &line[open..];
  7600	    let write = WRITE_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle)
  7601	        || (OPEN_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle)
  7602	            && OPEN_WRITE_FLAGS.iter().any(|flag| rest.contains(flag)));
  7603	    let wanted = if TWO_PATH_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle) {
  7604	        2
  7605	    } else {
  7606	        1
  7607	    };
  7608	    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(wanted);
  7609	    // The argument list, past the syscall name: without this the text before a
  7610	    // path reads `openat(7`, whose last comma-separated piece is the name
  7611	    // glued to the fd and parses as nothing.
  7612	    let args = &rest[needle.len()..];
  7613	    let mut cursor = args;
  7614	    let mut consumed = 0usize;
  7615	    for _ in 0..wanted {
  7616	        let Some(start) = cursor.find('"') else { break };
  7617	        let Some(end) = cursor[start + 1..].find('"') else {
  7618	            break;
  7619	        };
  7620	        let dirfd = args[..consumed + start]
  7621	            .rsplit(',')
  7622	            .find_map(|argument| argument.trim().parse::<i64>().ok());
  7623	        out.push((cursor[start + 1..start + 1 + end].to_owned(), write, dirfd));
  7624	        consumed += start + 1 + end + 1;
  7625	        cursor = &cursor[start + 1 + end + 1..];
  7626	    }
  7627	    out
  7628	}

  7705	            .and_then(|fd| open_fds.get(&(pid, fd)))

  7734	    returned_fd: Option<i64>,
  7735	    open_fds: &mut BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String>,
  7736	) {

  7744	fn duplicated_fd(line: &str, returned_fd: Option<i64>) -> Option<(i64, i64)> {
  7745	    let to = returned_fd.filter(|fd| *fd >= 0)?;
  7746	    let call = ["dup(", "dup2(", "dup3(", "fcntl("]
  7747	        .into_iter()
  7748	        .find(|name| line.contains(name))?;

  7750	        return None;
  7751	    }

  7753	    // first comma-separated piece is the source descriptor.
  7754	    let args = line.split_once(call)?.1;
  7755	    let from = args
  7756	        .split(',')
  7757	        .next()?
  7758	        .trim_end_matches(')')
  7759	        .trim()
  7760	        .parse::<i64>()
  7761	        .ok()?;
  7762	    Some((from, to))
  7763	}

  7765	fn record_chdir(
  7766	    line: &str,
  7767	    pid: u32,
  7768	    open_fds: &BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String>,
  7769	    cwds: &mut BTreeMap<u32, String>,

  7775	    // cwd and unanchored every relative path after it. It names a directory by
  7776	    // fd, so the pid moves wherever that fd was opened; an fd this trace never
  7777	    // saw opened leaves the cwd UNKNOWN rather than stale.

  7780	            .split_once("fchdir(")
  7781	            .and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split(')').next())
  7782	            .and_then(|token| token.trim().parse::<i64>().ok());

  7784	            Some(dir) => cwds.insert(pid, dir.clone()),
  7785	            None => cwds.remove(&pid),
  7786	        };
  7787	        return;
  7788	    }
  7789	    let Some((target, _)) = scope_trace_line_accesses(line).first().cloned() else {
  7790	        return;
  7791	    };

  7793	        target
  7794	    } else {
  7795	        cwds.get(&pid)
  7796	            .map_or_else(|| target.clone(), |cwd| format!("{cwd}/{target}"))
  7797	    };

  7799	}

  7803	/// was listed; `fchmod` names a descriptor and was not, so changing the locked

  7806	    line: &str,

  7824	        .next()?
  7825	        .trim()
  7826	        .parse::<i64>()
  7827	        .ok()?;

  7831	#[allow(
  7832	    clippy::too_many_lines,
  7833	    reason = "streaming trace scanner keeps fd, cwd, syscall and digest state in one pass"
  7834	)]
  7835	fn scan_scope_trace<R: std::io::BufRead>(mut reader: R) -> Result<ScopeTraceScan> {
  7836	    let mut scan = ScopeTraceScan::default();
  7837	    let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
  7838	    let mut buf = Vec::new();
  7839	    // Blind pass 1 at f360e90 (A07): `openat(AT_FDCWD, ".../heldout", O_DIRECTORY) = 7`
  7840	    // followed by `openat(7, "x.md", O_WRONLY)` named the locked corpus only on
  7841	    // the permitted read; the write carried no fragment. Directory fds are
  7842	    // remembered per pid from their open's return value, and a path relative
  7843	    // to one is judged under that directory. An `<unfinished ...>` open is
  7844	    // completed by its `<... openat resumed>) = fd` line.
  7845	    let mut open_fds: BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String> = BTreeMap::new();
  7846	    let mut unfinished: BTreeMap<u32, (String, bool)> = BTreeMap::new();
  7847	    // Blind pass 1 at aa00d41 (A07): a `chdir` into the locked corpus made
  7848	    // every later relative write nameless — no fragment, and resolution
  7849	    // against the repository root put it somewhere harmless. The cwd each pid
  7850	    // announces is remembered, and its relative paths resolve there.
  7851	    let mut cwds: BTreeMap<u32, String> = BTreeMap::new();
  7852	    loop {
  7853	        buf.clear();
  7854	        if reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut buf)? == 0 {
  7855	            break;
  7856	        }
  7857	        hasher.update(&buf);
  7858	        // Exactly `str::lines`: one trailing `\n`, then one `\r`, stripped.
  7859	        let line = buf.strip_suffix(b"\n").unwrap_or(&buf);
  7860	        let line = line.strip_suffix(b"\r").unwrap_or(line);
  7861	        let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(line);
  7862	        if scan.forbidden.is_none() {
  7863	            let lower = line.to_ascii_lowercase();
  7864	            scan.forbidden = FORBIDDEN_TRACE_FRAGMENTS
  7865	                .into_iter()
  7866	                .find(|fragment| lower.contains(fragment));
  7867	        }
  7868	        let mut tokens = line.splitn(2, ' ');
  7869	        if let Some(pid) = tokens.next().and_then(|token| token.parse::<u32>().ok()) {
  7870	            scan.pids.insert(pid);
  7871	            if tokens.next() == Some("+++ exited with 0 +++") {
  7872	                scan.exited_zero.insert(pid);
  7873	            }
  7874	            // A pid that exited holds no directory fds; a later process
  7875	            // reusing the number must not inherit them. Blind pass 1 at
  7876	            // `cbed339f` (A06): nor its working directory or a call it left
  7877	            // unfinished. Only the fds were dropped, so a process reusing the
  7878	            // number resolved its relative paths against the dead one's cwd.
  7879	            if line.contains(" +++ exited with ") || line.contains(" +++ killed by ") {
  7880	                open_fds.retain(|(owner, _), _| *owner != pid);
  7881	                cwds.remove(&pid);
  7882	                unfinished.remove(&pid);
  7883	            }
  7884	        }
  7885	        let pid = line
  7886	            .split(' ')
  7887	            .next()
  7888	            .and_then(|token| token.parse::<u32>().ok());
  7889	        let returned_fd = line
  7890	            .rsplit(" = ")
  7891	            .next()
  7892	            .and_then(|tail| tail.trim().parse::<i64>().ok());
  7893	        if let (Some(pid), true) = (pid, line.contains("<... openat resumed>"))
  7894	            && let (Some((path, is_dir)), Some(fd)) = (unfinished.remove(&pid), returned_fd)
  7895	        {
  7896	            if is_dir && fd >= 0 {
  7897	                open_fds.insert((pid, fd), path);
  7898	            } else {
  7899	                open_fds.remove(&(pid, fd));
  7900	            }
  7901	        }
  7902	        // Parsed ONCE and carried: `anchor_relative_paths` used to re-parse the
  7903	        // line and zip positionally against this vector, which is only safe
  7904	        // while the two parses agree on how many entries they yield (review of
  7905	        // `7e4ba39`). Passing the dirfds through removes the coupling.
  7906	        let mut arguments = scope_trace_line_arguments(&line);
  7907	        if let Some(pid) = pid {
  7908	            anchor_relative_paths(pid, &open_fds, &cwds, &mut arguments);
  7909	        }
  7910	        let mut accesses = arguments
  7911	            .into_iter()
  7912	            .map(|(path, write, _)| (path, write))
  7913	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  7914	        // Blind pass 1 at `ec045588` (A06): `chmod` and `fchmodat` name a
  7915	        // path and were listed; `fchmod` names a descriptor and was not, so
  7916	        // changing the locked corpus's mode or owner through an open
  7917	        // descriptor produced no write candidate at all. Every successful
  7918	        // open's path is already remembered for its fd, so the descriptor
  7919	        // resolves to the file it names.
  7920	        if let Some(pid) = pid
  7921	            && let Some(path) = fd_write_target(&line, pid, &open_fds)
  7922	        {
  7923	            accesses.push((path, true));
  7924	        }
  7925	        if let Some(pid) = pid {
  7926	            // Blind pass 1 at e09ae5e (A07): the cwd and dirfd maps are keyed
  7927	            // per pid and were never inherited, so a parent that chdir'd into
  7928	            // the locked corpus and then forked left the CHILD unanchored —
  7929	            // its relative write carried no forbidden text and resolved
  7930	            // against nothing. A child begins life with its parent's working
  7931	            // directory and its open descriptors.
  7932	            if let Some(child) = clone_child_pid(&line) {
  7933	                // A parent with no recorded cwd is at the trace's root, and so
  7934	                // is its child: whatever the map held for the child's number
  7935	                // belonged to an earlier process (A06, `cbed339f`).
  7936	                match cwds.get(&pid).cloned() {
  7937	                    Some(cwd) => cwds.insert(child, cwd),
  7938	                    None => cwds.remove(&child),
  7939	                };
  7940	                let inherited = open_fds
  7941	                    .range((pid, i64::MIN)..=(pid, i64::MAX))
  7942	                    .map(|((_, fd), dir)| (*fd, dir.clone()))
  7943	                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  7944	                for (fd, dir) in inherited {
  7945	                    open_fds.insert((child, fd), dir);
  7946	                }
  7947	            }
  7948	            record_chdir(&line, pid, &open_fds, &mut cwds);
  7949	            record_duplicated_fd(&line, pid, returned_fd, &mut open_fds);
  7950	            // Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A10): only `O_DIRECTORY` opens were
  7951	            // remembered, so a descriptor opened without it and later used as
  7952	            // a dirfd resolved against nothing. Every successful open's path
  7953	            // is remembered for its fd; one that is not a directory simply
  7954	            // never appears as a dirfd.
  7955	            if (line.contains("openat(") || line.contains("openat2(") || line.contains(" open("))
  7956	                && let Some((path, _)) = accesses.first()
  7957	            {
  7958	                if line.contains("<unfinished ...>") {
  7959	                    unfinished.insert(pid, (path.clone(), true));
  7960	                } else if let Some(fd) = returned_fd {
  7961	                    if fd >= 0 {
  7962	                        open_fds.insert((pid, fd), path.clone());
  7963	                    } else {
  7964	                        open_fds.remove(&(pid, fd));
  7965	                    }
  7966	                }
  7967	            }
  7968	        }
  7969	        for (path, write) in accesses {
  7970	            // Blind pass 1 at `6b36bbb9` (A02): candidates were collected only
  7971	            // when the path LOOKED like the corpus, so F-64's inode comparison
  7972	            // — added for exactly the case where it does not — never saw a
  7973	            // hard link under an unrelated name. Every write is a candidate;
  7974	            // the lexical rules still decide the lexical cases, and identity
  7975	            // decides the rest.
  7976	            if write {
  7977	                scan.locked_write_candidates.push(path.clone());
  7978	            }
  7979	            // Failed lookups remain write candidates above, so an attempted
  7980	            // mutation of locked data still refuses. They are excluded from
  7981	            // open-path and resolution digests: no kernel object was opened,
  7982	            // and canonicalization cannot authenticate a path that never
  7983	            // existed (ENOENT probes are common in tool discovery).
  7984	            if !scope_trace_line_failed(&line) {
  7985	                scan.open_paths.insert(path);
  7986	            }
  7987	        }
  7988	    }
  7989	    scan.raw_blake3 = hasher.finalize().to_hex().to_string();
  7990	    Ok(scan)
  7991	}

  8006	/// F-44 ruling (Brian, 2026-09-05). A stage may READ the locked corpus -- the
  8007	/// SLO graduation test measures the profile on it, which is why it is held
  8008	/// out -- but no stage may modify the repository's copy of it: the "never
  8009	/// hash-update" half of the lock, enforced on every trace. Copies under build
  8010	/// roots and scratch directories are outside the repository. The carved fuzz
  8011	/// binaries keep the full rule: their traces may not carry the fragment at
  8012	/// all (`ScopeTraceScan::forbidden`), because they are the one process family
  8013	/// whose evidence is about the corpus.
  8014	///
  8015	/// Relative paths are judged root-relative, conservatively: a stage's cwd is
  8016	/// not receipted, so a relative write that names the locked corpus refuses.
  8017	/// Every (device, inode) under the locked corpus. Blind pass 1 at `aeed70f9`
  8018	/// (A07): the write check resolved symlinks and pathname ancestry, and a hard
  8019	/// link is neither — it is a second name for the same inode, so writing
  8020	/// through one outside the corpus mutates corpus bytes under an innocent path.
  8021	/// Identity is read from directory metadata; no corpus file is opened.
  8022	fn locked_corpus_identities(root: &Utf8Path, within: &str) -> Result<BTreeSet<(u64, u64)>> {
  8023	    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;
  8024	    let corpora = root.join(within);
  8025	    let mut identities = BTreeSet::new();
  8026	    if !corpora.is_dir() {
  8027	        return Ok(identities);
  8028	    }
  8029	    let mut stack = vec![corpora];
  8030	    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
  8031	        // Review of `bba803d4`: skipping an unreadable directory returned a
  8032	        // partial set, and a hard link to a file inside it would then pass. A
  8033	        // corpus this cannot enumerate is a corpus it cannot protect.
  8034	        let entries = fs::read_dir(dir.as_std_path())
  8035	            .with_context(|| format!("enumerate the locked corpus at {dir}"))?;
  8036	        for entry in entries.flatten() {
  8037	            let path = entry.path();
  8038	            let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(&path)
  8039	                .with_context(|| format!("stat {} in the locked corpus", path.display()))?;
  8040	            if metadata.is_dir() {
  8041	                if let Ok(dir) = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(path) {
  8042	                    stack.push(dir);
  8043	                }
  8044	            } else if metadata.is_file() {
  8045	                identities.insert((metadata.dev(), metadata.ino()));
  8046	            }
  8047	        }
  8048	    }
  8049	    Ok(identities)
  8050	}

  8052	fn locked_corpus_write(
  8053	    root: &Utf8Path,
  8054	    candidates: &[String],
  8055	    label: &str,
  8056	) -> Result<Option<String>> {
  8057	    let canonical_root = fs::canonicalize(root.as_std_path())
  8058	        .with_context(|| format!("{label}: canonicalize repository root"))?;
  8059	    let identities = locked_corpus_identities(root, "conformance/corpora")?;
  8060	    for lexical in candidates {
  8061	        let path = Path::new(lexical);
  8062	        // Blind pass 1 at 78c8f9b (A12): a relative write from a subdirectory,
  8063	        // `../conformance/corpora/heldout/x`, joined onto the root climbed out
  8064	        // of it and passed. The cwd is not receipted, so a relative write that
  8065	        // names the locked corpus at all is refused, before any resolution.
  8066	        let lower = lexical.to_ascii_lowercase();
  8067	        if !path.is_absolute()
  8068	            && (lower.contains("conformance/corpora/") || lower.ends_with("conformance/corpora"))
  8069	        {
  8070	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  8071	        }
  8072	        let local = if path.is_absolute() {
  8073	            path.to_path_buf()
  8074	        } else {
  8075	            root.as_std_path().join(path)
  8076	        };
  8077	        // A path that no longer resolves (deleted after the trace) is judged
  8078	        // lexically: the conservative direction, since a lexical
  8079	        // conformance/corpora prefix still refuses.
  8080	        let canonical = canonicalize_trace_path(&local).unwrap_or(local);
  8081	        if let Ok(relative) = canonical.strip_prefix(&canonical_root)
  8082	            && relative
  8083	                .to_string_lossy()
  8084	                .to_ascii_lowercase()
  8085	                .starts_with("conformance/corpora")
  8086	        {
  8087	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  8088	        }
  8089	        // A07: a hard link is a second name for the same inode, so no amount
  8090	        // of path reasoning sees it. Identity does.
  8091	        if let Ok(metadata) = fs::symlink_metadata(&canonical) {
  8092	            use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;
  8093	            if identities.contains(&(metadata.dev(), metadata.ino())) {
  8094	                return Ok(Some(format!(
  8095	                    "{lexical} (hard link into the locked corpus)"
  8096	                )));
  8097	            }
  8098	        }
  8099	    }
  8100	    Ok(None)
  8101	}

  8281	/// Whether a relative traced path is left out of corpus resolution.
  8282	///
  8283	/// Relative paths are interpreted against the process cwd or a directory fd,
  8284	/// which the trace does not receipt; resolving one as root-relative can hide a
  8285	/// locked corpus behind a chdir or alias. A fuzz binary is invoked with an
  8286	/// absolute corpus path, so a relative one is the campaign's defect and refuses

  8288	/// index refresh, the campaign's seed manifest) and reviewer tooling opens
  8289	/// `../nvidia0` under /dev: unresolvable, and able to add no corpus entry, so

  8292	/// `locked_corpus_write`.

  8296	    locked: LockedCorpus,
  8297	    label: &str,
  8298	) -> Result<bool> {

  8300	        return Ok(false);
  8301	    }

  8303	        lexical_lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/") || lexical_lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/");

  8305	        LockedCorpus::AnyTouch if names_corpus => anyhow::bail!(
  8306	            "{label}: relative fuzz corpus path lacks authenticated cwd/dirfd binding"

  8309	        LockedCorpus::WritesOnly => Ok(true),

  8311	}

  8313	fn resolved_corpus_paths_digest_from(
  8314	    root: &Utf8Path,
  8315	    trace_root: &str,
  8316	    open_paths: &BTreeSet<String>,
  8317	    label: &str,
  8318	    access: CorpusAccess,
  8319	    locked: LockedCorpus,
  8320	) -> Result<String> {
  8321	    let canonical_root = fs::canonicalize(root.as_std_path())
  8322	        .with_context(|| format!("{label}: canonicalize repository root"))?;
  8323	    let trace_root = Path::new(trace_root);
  8324	    anyhow::ensure!(
  8325	        trace_root.is_absolute(),
  8326	        "{label}: trace_root must be absolute"
  8327	    );
  8328	    let mut resolved = BTreeSet::new();
  8329	    for lexical in open_paths {
  8330	        let lexical_path = Path::new(&lexical);
  8331	        let lexical_lower = lexical_path.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase();
  8332	        if relative_trace_path_is_skipped(lexical_path, &lexical_lower, locked, label)? {
  8333	            continue;
  8334	        }
  8335	        let under_trace_root =
  8336	            !lexical_path.is_absolute() || lexical_path.strip_prefix(trace_root).is_ok();
  8337	        if !under_trace_root {
  8338	            continue;
  8339	        }
  8340	        let local = trace_path_to_repo(root, trace_root, lexical)
  8341	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: cannot map traced repository path"))?;
  8342	        let canonical = canonicalize_trace_path(local.as_std_path())
  8343	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: traced repository path cannot be resolved"))?;
  8344	        let relative = canonical
  8345	            .strip_prefix(&canonical_root)
  8346	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: traced repository path escapes repository root"))?;
  8347	        let relative = relative.to_str().context("non-UTF-8 traced corpus path")?;
  8348	        let lower = relative.to_ascii_lowercase();
  8349	        if locked == LockedCorpus::AnyTouch {
  8350	            for forbidden in FORBIDDEN_TRACE_FRAGMENTS {
  8351	                anyhow::ensure!(
  8352	                    !lower.contains(forbidden),
  8353	                    "{label}: traced repository path resolves into forbidden data"
  8354	                );
  8355	            }
  8356	        }
  8357	        if lexical_lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/")
  8358	            || lexical_lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/")
  8359	            || lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/")
  8360	            || lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/")
  8361	        {
  8362	            resolved.insert(format!("{lexical}\0{relative}"));
  8363	        }
  8364	    }
  8365	    if access == CorpusAccess::Required {
  8366	        anyhow::ensure!(
  8367	            !resolved.is_empty(),
  8368	            "{label}: trace contains no resolvable fuzz corpus path"
  8369	        );
  8370	    }
  8371	    let resolved = resolved.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
  8372	    let resolved_bytes = format!("{}\n", resolved.join("\n"));
  8373	    Ok(blake3::hash(resolved_bytes.as_bytes()).to_hex().to_string())
  8374	}

  8376	/// Canonicalize the existing prefix of a traced path, then append historical
  8377	/// leaf components that libFuzzer may have deleted after opening them. This
  8378	/// preserves symlink and root-boundary checks without requiring every path in
  8379	/// a long-running trace to remain present at receipt time.
  8380	fn canonicalize_trace_path(path: &Path) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf> {
  8381	    let mut missing = Vec::new();
  8382	    let mut cursor = path;
  8383	    loop {
  8384	        match fs::symlink_metadata(cursor) {
  8385	            Ok(_) => break,
  8386	            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
  8387	                missing.push(
  8388	                    cursor
  8389	                        .file_name()
  8390	                        .context("traced path has no recoverable leaf")?
  8391	                        .to_owned(),
  8392	                );
  8393	                let leaf = missing.last().expect("just pushed missing leaf");
  8394	                anyhow::ensure!(
  8395	                    leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".") && leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".."),
  8396	                    "traced path contains a parent-directory suffix"
  8397	                );
  8398	                cursor = cursor
  8399	                    .parent()
  8400	                    .context("traced path has no existing ancestor")?;
  8401	                anyhow::ensure!(
  8402	                    cursor.file_name() != Some(std::ffi::OsStr::new("corpus")),
  8403	                    "traced path is missing a corpus entry; symlink history is unavailable"
  8404	                );
  8405	            }
  8406	            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
  8407	        }
  8408	    }
  8409	    let mut canonical = fs::canonicalize(cursor)?;
  8410	    for component in missing.into_iter().rev() {
  8411	        canonical.push(component);
  8412	    }
  8413	    Ok(canonical)
  8414	}

  7841	    // the permitted read; the write carried no fragment. Directory fds are
  7842	    // remembered per pid from their open's return value, and a path relative
  7843	    // to one is judged under that directory. An `<unfinished ...>` open is
  7844	    // completed by its `<... openat resumed>) = fd` line.
  7845	    let mut open_fds: BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String> = BTreeMap::new();
  7846	    let mut unfinished: BTreeMap<u32, (String, bool)> = BTreeMap::new();
  7847	    // Blind pass 1 at aa00d41 (A07): a `chdir` into the locked corpus made
  7848	    // every later relative write nameless — no fragment, and resolution
  7849	    // against the repository root put it somewhere harmless. The cwd each pid
  7850	    // announces is remembered, and its relative paths resolve there.
  7851	    let mut cwds: BTreeMap<u32, String> = BTreeMap::new();

  7853	        buf.clear();
  7854	        if reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut buf)? == 0 {
  7855	            break;
  7856	        }
  7857	        hasher.update(&buf);

  7859	        let line = buf.strip_suffix(b"\n").unwrap_or(&buf);

  7863	            let lower = line.to_ascii_lowercase();

  7865	                .into_iter()
  7866	                .find(|fragment| lower.contains(fragment));
  7867	        }

  7869	        if let Some(pid) = tokens.next().and_then(|token| token.parse::<u32>().ok()) {

  7875	            // reusing the number must not inherit them. Blind pass 1 at

  7877	            // unfinished. Only the fds were dropped, so a process reusing the

  7886	            .split(' ')
  7887	            .next()
  7888	            .and_then(|token| token.parse::<u32>().ok());

  7890	            .rsplit(" = ")
  7891	            .next()

  7930	            // against nothing. A child begins life with its parent's working

  7938	                    None => cwds.remove(&child),

  7941	                    .range((pid, i64::MIN)..=(pid, i64::MAX))
  7942	                    .map(|((_, fd), dir)| (*fd, dir.clone()))
  7943	                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();

  7945	                    open_fds.insert((child, fd), dir);
  7946	                }
  7947	            }
  7948	            record_chdir(&line, pid, &open_fds, &mut cwds);
  7949	            record_duplicated_fd(&line, pid, returned_fd, &mut open_fds);
  7950	            // Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A10): only `O_DIRECTORY` opens were
  7951	            // remembered, so a descriptor opened without it and later used as
  7952	            // a dirfd resolved against nothing. Every successful open's path
  7953	            // is remembered for its fd; one that is not a directory simply
  7954	            // never appears as a dirfd.
  7955	            if (line.contains("openat(") || line.contains("openat2(") || line.contains(" open("))

  7957	            {
  7958	                if line.contains("<unfinished ...>") {
  7959	                    unfinished.insert(pid, (path.clone(), true));
  7960	                } else if let Some(fd) = returned_fd {

  7965	                    }
  7966	                }
  7967	            }
  7968	        }

  7970	            // Blind pass 1 at `6b36bbb9` (A02): candidates were collected only
  7971	            // when the path LOOKED like the corpus, so F-64's inode comparison
  7972	            // — added for exactly the case where it does not — never saw a

  7975	            // decides the rest.
  7976	            if write {

  7980	            // mutation of locked data still refuses. They are excluded from
  7981	            // open-path and resolution digests: no kernel object was opened,
  7982	            // and canonicalization cannot authenticate a path that never
  7983	            // existed (ENOENT probes are common in tool discovery).

  7987	        }

  8006	/// F-44 ruling (Brian, 2026-09-05). A stage may READ the locked corpus -- the
  8007	/// SLO graduation test measures the profile on it, which is why it is held
  8008	/// out -- but no stage may modify the repository's copy of it: the "never
  8009	/// hash-update" half of the lock, enforced on every trace. Copies under build
  8010	/// roots and scratch directories are outside the repository. The carved fuzz
  8011	/// binaries keep the full rule: their traces may not carry the fragment at
  8012	/// all (`ScopeTraceScan::forbidden`), because they are the one process family
  8013	/// whose evidence is about the corpus.
  8014	///

  8016	/// not receipted, so a relative write that names the locked corpus refuses.

  8018	/// (A07): the write check resolved symlinks and pathname ancestry, and a hard
  8019	/// link is neither — it is a second name for the same inode, so writing
  8020	/// through one outside the corpus mutates corpus bytes under an innocent path.
  8021	/// Identity is read from directory metadata; no corpus file is opened.
  8022	fn locked_corpus_identities(root: &Utf8Path, within: &str) -> Result<BTreeSet<(u64, u64)>> {

  8026	    if !corpora.is_dir() {
  8027	        return Ok(identities);
  8028	    }

  8030	    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
  8031	        // Review of `bba803d4`: skipping an unreadable directory returned a
  8032	        // partial set, and a hard link to a file inside it would then pass. A
  8033	        // corpus this cannot enumerate is a corpus it cannot protect.
  8034	        let entries = fs::read_dir(dir.as_std_path())
  8035	            .with_context(|| format!("enumerate the locked corpus at {dir}"))?;
  8036	        for entry in entries.flatten() {
  8037	            let path = entry.path();
  8038	            let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(&path)
  8039	                .with_context(|| format!("stat {} in the locked corpus", path.display()))?;

  8041	                if let Ok(dir) = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(path) {
  8042	                    stack.push(dir);
  8043	                }
  8044	            } else if metadata.is_file() {
  8045	                identities.insert((metadata.dev(), metadata.ino()));
  8046	            }
  8047	        }
  8048	    }
  8049	    Ok(identities)
  8050	}

  8052	fn locked_corpus_write(
  8053	    root: &Utf8Path,

  8061	        let path = Path::new(lexical);
  8062	        // Blind pass 1 at 78c8f9b (A12): a relative write from a subdirectory,
  8063	        // `../conformance/corpora/heldout/x`, joined onto the root climbed out
  8064	        // of it and passed. The cwd is not receipted, so a relative write that
  8065	        // names the locked corpus at all is refused, before any resolution.
  8066	        let lower = lexical.to_ascii_lowercase();
  8067	        if !path.is_absolute()
  8068	            && (lower.contains("conformance/corpora/") || lower.ends_with("conformance/corpora"))
  8069	        {
  8070	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  8071	        }
  8072	        let local = if path.is_absolute() {
  8073	            path.to_path_buf()
  8074	        } else {
  8075	            root.as_std_path().join(path)
  8076	        };

  8078	        // lexically: the conservative direction, since a lexical
  8079	        // conformance/corpora prefix still refuses.
  8080	        let canonical = canonicalize_trace_path(&local).unwrap_or(local);
  8081	        if let Ok(relative) = canonical.strip_prefix(&canonical_root)
  8082	            && relative
  8083	                .to_string_lossy()
  8084	                .to_ascii_lowercase()
  8085	                .starts_with("conformance/corpora")
  8086	        {
  8087	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  8088	        }
  8089	        // A07: a hard link is a second name for the same inode, so no amount
  8090	        // of path reasoning sees it. Identity does.
  8091	        if let Ok(metadata) = fs::symlink_metadata(&canonical) {
  8092	            use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;

  8095	                    "{lexical} (hard link into the locked corpus)"

  8098	        }
  8099	    }

  8144	fn scan_scope_trace_union(
  8145	    root: &Utf8Path,
  8146	    row: &CorpusScopeTrace,
  8147	) -> Result<(ScopeTraceScan, BTreeSet<String>, Option<&'static str>)> {
  8148	    let label = format!("{} corpus scope", row.scope);
  8149	    let remainder_path = safe_repo_path(root, &row.trace, "corpus scope trace")?;
  8150	    let remainder = scan_scope_trace_file(&remainder_path, &label)?;

  8153	    // (F-44). Parts are the fuzz binaries: any fragment refuses.
  8154	    let mut forbidden = None;
  8155	    for part in &row.parts {
  8156	        let part_path = safe_repo_path(root, &part.trace, "corpus scope trace part")?;
  8157	        let scan = scan_scope_trace_file(&part_path, &label)?;
  8158	        require_eq(
  8159	            &format!(
  8160	                "{} corpus scope part {} trace_blake3",
  8161	                row.scope, part.trace
  8162	            ),
  8163	            &part.trace_blake3,
  8164	            &scan.raw_blake3,
  8165	        )?;

  8167	        // Blind pass 1 at `0a0b4b4b` (A07): the any-touch rule fired on the
  8168	        // lexical fragments `heldout` and `conformance/corpora`, so a hard
  8169	        // link under any other name was invisible — and F-64's inode
  8170	        // comparison guarded writes only, while the carved fuzz binaries are
  8171	        // the one family for which a READ is the leak. Identity applies to
  8172	        // every path a fuzz part opened.
  8173	        if forbidden.is_none() && corpus_identity_touched(root, &scan.open_paths)? {
  8174	            forbidden = Some("locked corpus reached by inode identity");
  8175	        }
  8176	        open.extend(scan.open_paths);
  8177	    }
  8178	    Ok((remainder, open, forbidden))

  8313	fn resolved_corpus_paths_digest_from(
  8314	    root: &Utf8Path,
  8315	    trace_root: &str,
  8316	    open_paths: &BTreeSet<String>,
  8317	    label: &str,
  8318	    access: CorpusAccess,
  8319	    locked: LockedCorpus,
  8320	) -> Result<String> {
  8321	    let canonical_root = fs::canonicalize(root.as_std_path())
  8322	        .with_context(|| format!("{label}: canonicalize repository root"))?;
  8323	    let trace_root = Path::new(trace_root);
  8324	    anyhow::ensure!(
  8325	        trace_root.is_absolute(),
  8326	        "{label}: trace_root must be absolute"
  8327	    );
  8328	    let mut resolved = BTreeSet::new();
  8329	    for lexical in open_paths {
  8330	        let lexical_path = Path::new(&lexical);
  8331	        let lexical_lower = lexical_path.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase();
  8332	        if relative_trace_path_is_skipped(lexical_path, &lexical_lower, locked, label)? {
  8333	            continue;
  8334	        }
  8335	        let under_trace_root =
  8336	            !lexical_path.is_absolute() || lexical_path.strip_prefix(trace_root).is_ok();
  8337	        if !under_trace_root {
  8338	            continue;
  8339	        }

  8341	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: cannot map traced repository path"))?;
  8342	        let canonical = canonicalize_trace_path(local.as_std_path())
  8343	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: traced repository path cannot be resolved"))?;
  8344	        let relative = canonical
  8345	            .strip_prefix(&canonical_root)
  8346	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: traced repository path escapes repository root"))?;
  8347	        let relative = relative.to_str().context("non-UTF-8 traced corpus path")?;
  8348	        let lower = relative.to_ascii_lowercase();
  8349	        if locked == LockedCorpus::AnyTouch {
  8350	            for forbidden in FORBIDDEN_TRACE_FRAGMENTS {
  8351	                anyhow::ensure!(
  8352	                    !lower.contains(forbidden),
  8353	                    "{label}: traced repository path resolves into forbidden data"
  8354	                );
  8355	            }
  8356	        }
  8357	        if lexical_lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/")
  8358	            || lexical_lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/")
  8359	            || lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/")
  8360	            || lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/")

  8367	            !resolved.is_empty(),
  8368	            "{label}: trace contains no resolvable fuzz corpus path"
  8369	        );
  8370	    }

  8376	/// Canonicalize the existing prefix of a traced path, then append historical
  8377	/// leaf components that libFuzzer may have deleted after opening them. This
  8378	/// preserves symlink and root-boundary checks without requiring every path in
  8379	/// a long-running trace to remain present at receipt time.
  8380	fn canonicalize_trace_path(path: &Path) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf> {
  8381	    let mut missing = Vec::new();
  8382	    let mut cursor = path;
  8383	    loop {
  8384	        match fs::symlink_metadata(cursor) {
  8385	            Ok(_) => break,
  8386	            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
  8387	                missing.push(
  8388	                    cursor
  8389	                        .file_name()
  8390	                        .context("traced path has no recoverable leaf")?
  8391	                        .to_owned(),
  8392	                );
  8393	                let leaf = missing.last().expect("just pushed missing leaf");
  8394	                anyhow::ensure!(
  8395	                    leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".") && leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".."),
  8396	                    "traced path contains a parent-directory suffix"
  8397	                );
  8398	                cursor = cursor
  8399	                    .parent()
  8400	                    .context("traced path has no existing ancestor")?;
  8401	                anyhow::ensure!(
  8402	                    cursor.file_name() != Some(std::ffi::OsStr::new("corpus")),
  8403	                    "traced path is missing a corpus entry; symlink history is unavailable"
  8404	                );
  8405	            }
  8406	            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
  8407	        }
  8408	    }
  8409	    let mut canonical = fs::canonicalize(cursor)?;
  8410	    for component in missing.into_iter().rev() {
  8411	        canonical.push(component);
  8412	    }
  8413	    Ok(canonical)
  8414	}
